record.original_question: Does every Parovichenko space have a c × c-independent matrix, where a Parovichenko space is a compact F-space of weight c in which every non-empty Gδ has infinite interior?

evidence.quote: Question 6. Does every Parovichenko space have a c × c-independent matrix?
A Parovichenko space is a compact F-space of weight c in which every non-empty Gδ has inﬁnite interior.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum. A compact Hausdorff space $X$ is called an $F$-space if every cozero subset of $X$ is $C^*$-embedded in $X$ (equivalently, disjoint cozero sets have disjoint closures). The weight of $X$ is the minimum cardinality of a base for its topology. A Parovichenko space is a compact Hausdorff $F$-space of weight $\mathfrak{c}$ in which every nonempty $G_\delta$-subset has nonempty (equivalently, infinite) interior.

Given a Parovichenko space $X$, a $\mathfrak{c} \times \mathfrak{c}$-independent matrix on $X$ is a family $\{A_{\alpha,\beta} : \alpha < \mathfrak{c},\ \beta < \mathfrak{c}\}$ of nonempty clopen subsets of $X$ such that:
(i) for each $\alpha < \mathfrak{c}$, the sets $\{A_{\alpha,\beta} : \beta < \mathfrak{c}\}$ are pairwise disjoint; and
(ii) for every finite function $\sigma : \mathfrak{c} \to \mathfrak{c}$ with finite domain $F \subset \mathfrak{c}$, the intersection $\bigcap_{\alpha \in F} A_{\alpha,\sigma(\alpha)}$ has nonempty interior (equivalently, is nonempty and clopen-nontrivial).

Question: Does every Parovichenko space admit a $\mathfrak{c} \times \mathfrak{c}$-independent matrix?
